name: The Cells on the Paper
description: On an endless checkered sheet of paper, $$$n$$$ cells are chosen and colored in three colors, where $$$n$$$ is divisible by $$$3$$$. It turns out that there are exactly $$$\frac{n}{3}$$$ marked cells of each of three colors! Find the largest such $$$k$$$ that it's possible to choose $$$\frac{k}{3}$$$ cells of each color, remove all other marked cells, and then select three rectangles with sides parallel to the grid lines so that the following conditions hold: No two rectangles can intersect (but they can share a part of the boundary). In other words, the area of intersection of any two of these rectangles must be $$$0$$$. The $$$i$$$-th rectangle contains all the chosen cells of the $$$i$$$-th color and no chosen cells of other colors, for $$$i = 1, 2, 3$$$.
input_specification: The first line of the input contains a single integer $$$n$$$ — the number of the marked cells ($$$3 \leq n \le 10^5$$$, $$$n$$$ is divisible by 3). The $$$i$$$-th of the following $$$n$$$ lines contains three integers $$$x_i$$$, $$$y_i$$$, $$$c_i$$$ ($$$|x_i|,|y_i| \leq 10^9$$$; $$$1 \leq c_i \leq 3$$$), where $$$(x_i, y_i)$$$ are the coordinates of the $$$i$$$-th marked cell and $$$c_i$$$ is its color. It's guaranteed that all cells $$$(x_i, y_i)$$$ in the input are distinct, and that there are exactly $$$\frac{n}{3}$$$ cells of each color.
output_specification: Output a single integer $$$k$$$ — the largest number of cells you can leave.
approach_summary: Verify predicate monotonicity: P(x) is true for x ≤ K and false otherwise. Binary search over the answer domain to find the boundary in O(log(Range) × Verify_Time).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1608E — The Cells on the Paper [33. Binary Search]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary search on the monotonic answer domain.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The predicate function $P(x)$ ('Is answer $\le x$ feasible?') is monotonic: if $P(x)$ is true for some value, it remains true for all larger values (or vice versa). This allows binary division of the answer search space $[\text{low}, \text{high}]$ in $O(\log(\text{Range}))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N \log(\text{Range}))$
  The binary search divides the search interval by 2 at each iteration, requiring $\log_2(\text{Range})$ steps. In each step, the feasibility check `check(mid)` scans the array in $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(1)$ auxiliary space
  The algorithm operates directly over the input array without allocating extra auxiliary memory.
